Apple has reportedly been working with LG on a "second-party" Home accessory, but the latest leak shows another company is also launching a "second-party" smart home product.

iOS 27.2 code reveals new Home accessories will debut as "second-party," not manufactured by LG

Over the past day, multiple leaks have surfaced about Apple's ambitions to expand its smart home ecosystem.

In addition to the first-party Home products expected to debut next week, including the new Apple TV 4K, "HomePad," and HomePod mini 2, the company is also reportedly collaborating with LG on a range of new home accessories.

These accessories are co-developed by Apple and LG, but will be sold under the LG brand. Images leaked today reveal what they look like:

  • Leaked images reveal Apple-designed smart door lock, thermostat, and other products for LG
  • Apple and LG's new Home camera and doorbell surface in leaked images

It makes sense for Apple to strengthen its smart home ecosystem through collaborative product development. And indeed, such partnerships may not be limited to LG alone.

Leaker pdfu discovered two additional Home accessories in iOS 27.2, also tagged as "second-party" products.

These two accessories are a Schneider-branded smart thermostat and a temperature/humidity sensor.

According to pdfu's article, currently in Apple's HomeKit database, only the new LG accessories and these two Schneider products carry the "second-party" label.

Accessories classified as second-party receive "special treatment" from the operating system.

It's not yet known whether Apple is working as closely with Schneider as it is with LG to develop accessories. However, the code does hint at this possibility.

What do you think of Apple's reported new Home product strategy? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
